subject.title: fix: harden security and release integrity

question: Should self-hosted ClickClack installations have an explicit administrator-controlled path for trusted private-network callbacks, or is public-only callback egress the permanent supported contract?
rationale: The strict policy closes an SSRF boundary but intentionally removes an existing self-hosted integration mode, so the permanent trust and upgrade contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Secure default with allowlist
options.body: Reject private destinations by default while allowing administrators to opt specific trusted hosts or CIDRs into callback egress.

options.title: Public-only contract
options.body: Keep the unconditional block and explicitly document the breaking upgrade behavior for existing private callbacks.

options.title: Split callback hardening
options.body: Land the unrelated hardening separately while the callback network contract receives focused design and review.

recommendation.title: Secure default with allowlist
recommendation.body: Reject private destinations by default while allowing administrators to opt specific trusted hosts or CIDRs into callback egress.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the callback implementation and are the strongest evidenced repository member for carrying the chosen policy through code and tests.
